concept.title: Read the caller-visible contract
paragraphs: Start with the receiver, input types, return type, and accessibility. A return type promises what a successful caller receives; it does not hide failure meaning.
Use IntelliSense one parameter or member at a time rather than memorizing a dense signature.

concept.title: Modern does not automatically mean clearer
paragraphs: Prefer the form that makes this business rule easiest to read and maintain. Older or more explicit syntax can remain the better teaching or production choice.
Compiler diagnostics identify unsupported language versions, inaccessible members, missing required values, and unsafe nullable paths.

lab.title: Generics, Lambdas, and LINQ
lab.objective: Trace how generics, lambdas, and LINQ cooperate in a type-safe business pipeline.
lab.task: Filter and total a typed collection of purchase lines.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/refreshers/r2 from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/refreshers/r2. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/refreshers/r2/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Filter and total a typed collection of purchase lines.
Step 4/12: Create PurchaseLine as a sealed record containing product, quantity, and unit price.
Step 5/12: Create List<PurchaseLine>; read T as PurchaseLine throughout the collection API.
Step 6/12: Call Where with a lambda that keeps positive quantities.
Step 7/12: Read Func<PurchaseLine,bool> as one PurchaseLine in and one Boolean decision out.
Step 8/12: Call Select to project each surviving line to decimal line total.
Step 9/12: Store the deferred IEnumerable<decimal>, then call Sum to execute and collapse it.
Step 10/12: Run and verify the total without relying on another refresher.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/refreshers/r2 --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/refreshers/r2 --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
